title: Liver and Bacon
subtitle: Calves' liver with smoked bacon, onion, and gravy
excerpt: Calves' liver sliced thin and fried quickly until just pink, served with crispy smoked bacon, caramelised onion, and a rich pan gravy. A British classic that must be cooked fast.

recipe.sourceNotes: Liver and bacon is one of the oldest British meat dishes, eaten since medieval times when offal was prized as the most nutritious part of the animal. Calves' liver is the most tender and mildest-flavoured variety and is the standard choice for this dish; lamb's liver is stronger and slightly more bitter but also good and cheaper. The key technique is speed: liver must be cooked quickly over very high heat until just pink in the centre. Overcooked liver becomes grey, grainy, and strongly flavoured in a way that puts many people off. The caramelised onion provides sweetness to balance the iron flavour of the liver. Serve with mashed potato or crusty bread to absorb the gravy.

content.text: Liver must be sliced no thicker than 1 cm for it to cook through in the time needed for the outside to colour. Season it with salt just before it goes into the pan, not in advance, or it draws moisture and will steam rather than fry. Cook in batches if the pan is not wide enough: crowding causes steaming. The liver is done when the last trace of pink just disappears from the centre and the juices run clear.

items.preparation: sliced 1 cm thick; or use lamb's liver

content.text: Fry the bacon in the dry frying pan over medium-high heat until crisp. Remove and keep warm. Add a splash of oil and fry the onion in the same pan over medium heat for 15 minutes until soft and golden. Remove and keep warm.

Increase to high heat. Add the remaining oil. Season the liver with salt and pepper just before cooking. Dust lightly with flour on both sides. Fry for 1 to 2 minutes per side until browned on the outside but just pink within. Work in batches. Remove and keep warm.

Pour the red wine into the hot pan and let it bubble, scraping up the browned bits. Add the stock, Worcestershire sauce, and thyme. Simmer for 3 minutes until slightly reduced. Taste for seasoning. Serve the liver and bacon on a bed of caramelised onion with the gravy poured over. Scatter with parsley.
